To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temperature dependence of heavy quark drag is responsible for a part of the $R_{\rm AA}$ and $v_{\rm 2}$ puzzle; a decreasing drag coefficient is not sufficient to describe the experimental data; a non-decreasing drag is required for a simultaneous description.

the $R_{\rm AA}(p_T)$-$v_2(p_{\rm T})$ puzzle is solved by the temperature dependence of heavy quark transport coefficients in the QGP, which can be constrained by a combination of $R_{\text{AA}}(p_{T})$, $v_2$, and the $p_T$-broadening.
the heavy quark transport properties, especially the temperature dependence of heavy quark drag coefficients, are responsible for the observed puzzle between $R_{AA}$(pT) and v2(pT).

the study of heavy quark transport coefficients in QCD.
a better understanding of the QGP medium properties by studying the heavy quark transport in the medium.
the study of the temperature dependence of heavy quark drag and diffusion coefficients in a QGP medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy quark transport coefficients, especially the drag, play a key role in the description of the heavy quarks in the quark gluon plasmas.

the $v_2/p_T$ for heavy quarks is not yet understood and it is not possible to draw a definite conclusion about the heavy quark energy loss mechanism from the existing data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $R_{\rm AA}(p_T)$ vs. $v_2 (p_T)$ puzzle for heavy quark probes is solved if one considers a non-decreasing drag and diffusion coefficients in a temperature range $T_c\leq T \leq 2T_c$.
the $R_{ AA} $ and $v_ 2 $ puzzle can be solved for heavy quarks by a non-decreasing drag as $ T \, \to \, T_c \,$.
, for a simultaneous description for $R_{AA} \, and \, v_2$ for heavy quarks at RHIC and the LHC energies, the temperature dependence of heavy quark transport coefficients must be considered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heavy quarks can be used to probe the temperature dependence of heavy quark diffusion and drag coefficients in the QGP.
a non-decreasing drag as $ T \to\ T_c \, $ can be a major ingredient for the simultaneous description of $v_2\, $ and $R_{AA}\, $ for heavy quark observables.
the temperature dependence of heavy quark diffusion coefficients is a key ingredient to understand the heavy flavor observables in the heavy-ion collisions.
